prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows the camera wearer inside a rectangular metal-mesh enclosure with a raised concrete platform below, looking closely through the left mesh wall (~0.3 to 0.6 m away) toward a sloped dirt mound (~1 to 2 m away) and tree trunks (~2 to 4 m away) in frames 1 to 3, before turning right in frames 4 and 5 to look lengthwise down the ~2.5-metre-long cage interior. In frame 3, the wearer's right hand enters the lower foreground at ~0.3 m within arm's reach to touch the left mesh wall, while in frames 4 and 5 a low white-brick barrier sits at the far end of the concrete platform (~2.5 m ahead) with brick piles and a standing person beyond the far mesh wall (~3.5 to 4.5 m away, facing and looking toward the camera wearer). Across the five frames, the left mesh remains within arm's reach as the wearer pivots their head and body roughly 90 degrees clockwise from facing the left wall to facing the front end of the enclosure. Compared to the visually busy RGB strip where sunlit foliage, brick piles, and shadows blend with the dark bars, the depth map clearly isolates the foreground mesh grid, the receding planar gradient of the concrete floor, and the close proximity of the wearer's hand. However, the depth map is unreliable for objects seen through the finer distant mesh in frames 4 and 5, where the standing person and brick piles beyond the far wall are merged into an indistinct dark background.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is almost entirely blank across all five frames, detecting only a single purple mask in the lower-centre of frame 3 where the camera wearer's right hand reaches up to touch the metal mesh at ~0.3 m distance. With the RGB strip for context, the scene actually contains the camera wearer's hand within arm's reach in frame 3, a metal cage enclosure surrounding a concrete slab (~0.3 to 2.5 m away), surrounding dirt and brick piles (~1 to 4 m away), and a person standing ~3.5 to 4.5 m away behind the far cage wall and brick pile in frames 4 and 5 facing toward the camera wearer. As the camera wearer turns right from facing the left mesh wall (frames 1 to 3) to looking down the cage corridor (frames 4 and 5), the hand leaves the field of view and the distant person comes into view, partly occluded by the cage mesh and bricks. While the mask in frame 3 sharply delineates the silhouette of the wearer's foreground hand and extended index finger against the cluttered dirt background, the map provides no spatial information in the remaining frames. It is highly unreliable here, misclassifying the wearer's hand as a 'fire hydrant' and completely failing to segment the distant person in frames 4 and 5 due to heavy occlusion by the wire mesh.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely black across all five frames, failing to detect either the camera wearer's reaching right hand in frame 3 or the distant standing person in frames 4 and 5. In the RGB strip, the camera wearer looks left through the cage mesh (~0.3 to 0.6 m away, within arm's reach) in frames 1 to 3, raises their right hand into the lower-centre foreground at ~0.3 m with an extended index finger touching a mesh bar in frame 3, and then turns right in frames 4 and 5 to face down the ~2.5 m concrete enclosure. In frames 4 and 5, another person stands upright ~3.5 to 4.5 m in front of the camera wearer beyond the far mesh wall and a pile of red bricks (~1 m behind the low brick wall at the end of the cage), facing and looking toward the camera wearer while holding a long-handled tool, with their lower body occluded by the bricks and their entire figure partially occluded by the cage grid. Nothing is revealed by the pose map that is hard to see in the RGB alone, because no yellow body or magenta hand skeletons are rendered in any frame. The pose map is completely unreliable in this scene, missing the close-up egocentric hand in frame 3 due to self-occlusion and dark lighting against the soil, and missing the person in frames 4 and 5 due to distance and occlusion from the intervening wire mesh.
